key_insight: LongE2V shows that a pre-trained video diffusion model can be adapted to event streams to reconstruct, predict, and interpolate video over long horizons with sharper details and better stability than regression-based methods.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of converting sparse event camera data into high-quality video, especially when the goal is long-term reconstruction, future frame prediction, and frame interpolation without blur or temporal drift.
method: Fine-tunes a foundational video diffusion model instead of training a generative model from scratch, improving data efficiency.
Uses event streams as conditioning to jointly support video reconstruction, prediction, and frame interpolation in one framework.
Introduces an autoregressive strategy to maintain temporal consistency over longer sequences and reduce long-horizon instability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, LongE2V offers a practical path to high-quality event-based video generation with less training data and stronger perceptual realism. It is especially relevant for applications needing robust motion recovery in challenging, low-light, or high-speed sensing settings.

paper_title: LongE2V: Long-Horizon Event-based Video Reconstruction, Prediction, and Frame Interpolation with Video Diffusion Models
